title: Convergence-order plot (plotting code)
oracle_notes:
with `h=[0.2,0.1,0.05,0.025]` and `err=0.3*h**2*(1±1%)`, the returned order is
within 0.05 of 2, both axes are log scale, and the figure contains a text annotation
and a legend.
figure_note: `plot_convergence(h, err)` as the oracle called it, on its test data: h = 0.2, 0.1, 0.05, 0.025 and err = 0.3·h² with ±1% alternating noise (true order 2). Rendered by the grader with matplotlib (Agg, 150 dpi).

title: Silo (calculus word problem)
oracle_notes: 9.8 h. Key step: V = 0.75π h³, so dh/dt = 60000π / (2.25π h²). Automatic: the ANSWER line only; the judge checks the cone volume.

title: Simpson's rule and observed order
oracle_notes:
S10 = 0.693150 (6 d.p.), error at n=10 about 3.05e-6, observed order within
3.8 to 4.2, theory says 4. Automatic: S10, observed order, and the `THEORY_ORDER: 4` line.

title: Does this ODE need a stiff solver?
oracle_notes:
a printed number within 1e-3 relative of `exp(-10)` (the prompt asks for 6 significant figures; scipy's default tolerances give about 7e-3). Reasoning check: the model notices the
right-hand side simplifies exactly to `-y`, so it is not stiff. Penalize "it has a
coefficient of 1000, use Radau" without simplifying. Automatic: the printed number and the `STIFF: no` line; the judge checks the
reason given.

title: Householder QR for least squares
oracle_notes:
`||QR-A||/||A||<1e-13`, `||QᵀQ-I||<1e-13`, QR residual matches
`np.linalg.lstsq` to 1e-10. Reference residuals: QR 1.7e-13, normal equations 1.1e-6.
Explanation should mention that forming AᵀA squares the condition number. Automatic: the numbers above, and no library qr/lstsq called by
`householder_qr` or `lstsq_qr` (a self-test under `__main__` may use them); the judge checks the explanation.

title: Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights by Newton's method
oracle_notes:
for n=64, nodes and weights match `leggauss` to 1e-13, and the rule integrates
`exp(x)` on [-1,1] to within 1e-14 of `e - 1/e`. Weight formula:
`w = 2 / ((1-x²) P_n'(x)²)`. Automatic: also no leggauss/roots_legendre called by `gauss_legendre`.

title: Positivity-preserving nonlinear conduction (solver)
oracle_notes:
∑u conserved to 1e-12 relative; `min(u) >= 1` (maximum principle); N=200
vs N=400 (cell-averaged) differ by under 5e-3 in RMS (reference gives 5e-6). Timestep:
`dt = cfl*dx²/(2*max κ)` with cfl ≤ 1. The judge checks the stated restriction uses max κ.

title: Linear Hasegawa-Mima waves (derive, then implement)
oracle_notes:
ω = -v* ky / (1+k²), exact φ = cos(kx x + ky y + v* ky t/(1+k²)). Relative L2
error below 1e-6 (reference gives 1.4e-8). Penalize a wrong sign of ω or missing the
`1+k²` denominator. Automatic: `omega()` evaluated at four points (one with v*≠1) and the solver error;
the judge checks the derivation.

title: Dipole with a source surface (derive, then code)
oracle_notes:
with `den = 1 + 2 R_ss³`,
`B_r = B0 (1 + 2R_ss³/r³)/den · cosθ`, `B_θ = -B0 (1 - R_ss³/r³)/den · sinθ`.
Checks: `B_r(1,θ)=B0 cosθ`, `B_θ(R_ss,θ)=0`, div and curl below 1e-8 (reference
about 1e-11). `B_r(R_ss, 0) ≈ 0.09302`.

title: Find the bugs (review, short output)
oracle_notes:
two bugs. (a) the timestep uses the mean of κ instead of the max, which
violates the stability limit near the peak and the solution goes negative and blows up
(reference: min u about -2.5e6). (b) the right boundary flux is copied from the interior
instead of set to zero, so heat leaks out and ∑u is not conserved (reference drift
2.9e-6). The fixed version conserves ∑u to 1e-12 and stays at min u >= 1. Score each bug
separately. The code checks cover both fixes; the judge checks the explanations.
